ex: My grandfather is a war veteran.
The veterans got free tickets today.
We thanked the veterans at the parade.
She is a veteran of the army.
veteran.note: Also means a person with long experience: a veteran teacher.

ex: I live on campus this year.
The library is in the middle of campus.
Can you show me around the campus?
There is a nice cafe on campus.
Let's meet at the bar after work.
The bar closes at midnight.
We had a drink at a small bar.
Is there a good bar near here?
Ha! I knew you were wrong!
Ha, that's a funny joke!
"Ha ha, very funny," she said.
Ha! I won the game again!
ha.note: "Ha ha" shows laughing; it can also mean you are not amused.

ex: I buy fresh fruit at the market.
The market is open on Saturdays.
Let's go to the market for vegetables.
Is there a market near your house?
market.note: For a big food shop, people usually say "supermarket" or "grocery store".

ex: This is her debut album.
He made his debut in the film last year.
Their debut song was a big hit.
The band played their debut show here.
She is the founder of the company.
The founder started the shop in 2010.
I met the founder at a meeting.
The founders were two young friends.
Look for the word in the index.
The index is at the back of the book.
Check the index to find the page.
This book has a very long index.
I'd like chicken with rice, please.
We eat rice almost every day.
Can you cook the rice for dinner?
This rice is too salty.
rice.note: Uncountable: some rice, not "a rice" or "rices".

ex: We did a fun experiment in class.
The experiment didn't work this time.
Let's try a simple experiment at home.
The kids loved the science experiment.
Don't be an idiot!
I felt like an idiot at the meeting.
Some idiot parked in my space.
I'm such an idiot, I forgot my keys!
idiot.note: Rude word; be careful using it about other people.

ex: Do you want to play baseball?
We watched a baseball game on TV.
My son loves baseball.
He wears a baseball cap every day.
The minimum age is 18.
You need a minimum of two hours.
Keep the noise to a minimum, please.
What is the minimum price for this?
Can I see your ID, please?
I forgot my ID at home.
You need a photo ID to enter.
Please show your student ID.
ID.note: Say each letter: "eye-dee". It means an identity card or document.

ex: She is a great athlete.
The athletes train every morning.
He wants to be a professional athlete.
Many athletes eat a lot of protein.
He scored one goal and two assists.
Thanks for the assist on that goal!
She had five assists in the game.
That was a great assist!
My uncle is a pilot.
The pilot said, "Welcome on board."
She wants to be a pilot one day.
The pilot landed the plane safely.
We saw a tiger at the zoo.
The tiger is sleeping in the sun.
Tigers are big and strong.
My son drew a tiger at school.
What are your symptoms?
A fever is a common symptom of flu.
Call the doctor if the symptoms get worse.
I have no symptoms today.
I got a bonus at work this year.
Workers get a bonus in December.
The free coffee is a nice bonus.
Did you get your bonus yet?
The jinn came out of the lamp.
In the story, a jinn grants three wishes.
My kids love stories about jinn.
The old book tells tales of jinn.
jinn.note: In fairy tales people usually say "genie". Jinn is often also the plural.

ex: She won a gold medal.
He showed us his medal.
Our team got a silver medal.
Every runner got a medal at the end.
My sister is a fashion designer.
We need a designer for our website.
The designer made a new logo for us.
He works as a game designer.
There was a big protest in the city.
Many students went to the protest.
The protest was peaceful.
The road is closed because of a protest.
The critics loved the new film.
She is a food critic.
The critic gave the movie four stars.
My dad is my biggest critic.
critic.note: A critic is a person; the article or opinion is a review.

ex: Our opponent is a strong team.
She shook hands with her opponent.
He beat his opponent in two games.
Who is your next opponent?
She works as a TV reporter.
A reporter asked me some questions.
The reporters waited outside the building.
He wants to be a sports reporter.
That's a good argument.
What is your main argument?
His argument made sense to me.
I don't agree with your argument.
argument.note: Also often means a fight with words: "We had an argument."

ex: Turn off the gas after cooking.
We cook on a gas stove.
I can smell gas in the kitchen.
Our gas bill is high this month.
gas.note: In American English "gas" also often means fuel for a car (gasoline).

ex: The jury liked her song best.
The jury chose the winner.
She was on the jury at the film festival.
The jury gave him first place.
jury.note: Most often means people who decide a case in a court.

ex: I think I have a virus.
My computer has a virus.
The doctor said it's just a virus.
Install this app to stop viruses.
Thanks for your quick reply.
I'm still waiting for a reply.
Her reply made me laugh.
Read the replies under my post.
We saw a celebrity at the airport.
She wants to be a celebrity.
Many celebrities live in this area.
I took a photo with a celebrity!
She is the CEO of a big company.
The CEO will speak at the meeting.
Our CEO sent an email to everyone.
He became CEO last year.
CEO.note: Say each letter: C-E-O. It means the top boss of a company.

ex: We need an investor for our business.
The investors liked our idea.
He is a small investor in tech.
She met with two investors today.
She has a strong character.
He is a man of good character.
My dog has a funny character.
Kind words show your character.
character.note: For everyday talk, "personality" is more common. Also means a person in a story.

ex: That's bullshit, and you know it.
I don't believe his bullshit.
Stop telling me bullshit!
This story sounds like bullshit.
bullshit.note: Very rude slang; don't use it at work or with strangers. Polite: nonsense.

ex: That's a super idea!
The party was super fun.
Thanks, you're super nice.
I'm super tired today.
super.note: Informal. Often used before adjectives to mean "very": super easy.

ex: We visited an old palace in the city.
The king lived in this palace.
The palace has a beautiful garden.
Can we take photos inside the palace?
I asked my question on a forum.
This forum has good tips for travelers.
Read the forum before you post.
I found the answer in an online forum.
The shop is on Fifth Avenue.
Turn left onto the avenue.
We live on a busy avenue.
Walk two blocks down the avenue.
avenue.note: In addresses it is often short: Ave.

ex: She makes content for social media.
I like the content on this channel.
We post new content every week.
This website has great free content.
content.note: Uncountable: "a lot of content", not "contents". Stress the first part: CON-tent.

ex: Send the file in PDF format.
What format is this video?
I don't like the new format of the show.
Please use this format for your report.
Public transport is cheap here.
I use public transport every day.
What transport do you take to work?
Transport in this city is very good.
transport.note: In American English "transportation" is more common: public transportation.

ex: The audio is too quiet.
I can't hear the audio on the video.
Check your audio before the call.
I listen to audio books in the car.
Our team made the playoffs!
We watched the playoff game together.
They lost in the first playoff round.
The playoffs start next week.
